title: Circuit-aware readiness policy and scaled failover playbook
creator: Asha Banerjee
description: Deliver a production-ready readiness/liveness strategy that is aware of circuit-breaker state and request shape so autoscaling decisions and multi-region failover preserve SLOs. Current readiness checks are binary and cause thrashing during partial regional degradations; we need layered readiness, a circuit-aware gating layer, and a playbook to scale and fail over gracefully without violating P99 and availability SLOs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Readiness endpoint exposes tiered health: GREEN/YELLOW/DEGRADED/RED and a compact numeric score for admission controllers.
- Autoscaler integration consumes score and applies hysteresis windows to avoid oscillation.
- Circuit controller can mark routes as "DEGRADED" and trigger token-weighted load shedding paths.
- Runbook exists: steps for oncall to perform manual failovers and safe rollbacks.
- End-to-end test harness simulates regional capacity loss and demonstrates SLO preservation for 95% of runs.
design_notes:
We prototyped a 0-100 health score combining: local queue length (normalized by configured concurrency), recent 99th latency delta vs baseline, token burn rate, and probe success ratio. The circuit controller maps score thresholds to readiness tiers. Important trade-offs: keeping probes lightweight to avoid cold-path amplification; capturing request-shape signals without introducing probe fanout; prefer sampled synthetic traces rather than broad live traffic sampling. We will implement an admission wrapper that refuses new sessions at YELLOW but drains existing ones, and refuses both at RED.

Key design decisions: use a compact numeric score (int8) to make signals cheap across the fleet; apply per-route token weights so high-cost requests are throttled first; implement backoff with exponential windows that are jittered per node to break synchronization.

See design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/projects/REGIONRES/portal/CARD-736 (internal).
implementation_plan:
1) Extend health endpoint to return score + tier (2 days). 2) Add circuit controller module to gateway that listens to health scores and route-level shard metrics (3 days). 3) Modify autoscaler hook to ingest score and apply hysteresis + derating (2 days). 4) Implement token-weighted shedding in request router with config-driven weights (3 days). 5) Integrate canary warmup policy for new nodes to avoid readiness flips (2 days). 6) End-to-end system tests and chaos scenarios (4 days).

Progress: Implemented step 1 and initial schema for score. Gateway stub merged (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/1823).
rollout_plan: Phase A (canary): enable new health scoring in staging and deploy to 5% of capacity in us-central and eu-west. Run synthetic partial-region-loss tests and collect SLO metrics for 48h. Phase B (regional ramp): enable token-weighted shedding and autoscale gating in two non-critical clusters for 1 week. Phase C (global): flip policy on in all regions with 24h monitoring guardrails and automatic rollback if P99 latency regression > 10% or error rate increase > 0.5%.
telemetry_requirements: shed.events (counter) with labels: route, region, weight_class
test_plan:
- Unit tests for score calc with synthetic histograms.
- Integration tests: kube-probe emulation and gate transitions.
- Chaos tests: kill 30% of nodes in a region and validate no SLO violations across 20 runs.
- Load tests: mixed request shapes with a 80/20 split between short and long-running tokens for 2 hours.
- Oncall drills: simulate manual failover following runbook.
blockers:
- Need updated autoscaler API support to accept an external readiness score (ENG-110045 is in review).
- Final agreement on token-weight taxonomy from product (pending PM review).
updates: 2026-01-22: Initial design sketch reviewed with SRE and infra; decided on numeric health score instead of multi-boolean gates.
2026-02-05: Completed health schema and added lightweight sampling to reduce probe fanout; merged gateway stub PR.
2026-02-18: Prototype autoscaler hook accepted; still waiting on autoscaler API change rollout window (blocked by ENG-110045).
2026-03-03: Implemented token-weighted shedding prototype behind feature flag; internal load tests show 12% lower P99 impact under simulated region throttling.
2026-03-10: Began Phase A canary in staging clusters; collecting telemetry; no SLO regressions observed in first 12 hours.
